answer: One body, one identity: each identity needs a fresh blood-donation record; the body sets a 56-day recovery limit, so one donor backs one identity. The vertex: donor state ID plus a chair-side photo, checked live against the registry; duplicates rejected. Each fake costs one donation: 350 ml of nectar, 150 units in fees, a 56-day wait. 100 fakes need 100 real donors, 15,000 units, 5,600 donor-days. Cheapest cheat: paying a stand-in to donate under a false name — the registry public beacon of hashed donor IDs exposes reused records, and a caught stand-in loses eligibility plus fraud charges.
